body:
What is SEO! A highly searched expression in search engines. In this article you will learn exactly how to reach the first position in Google, even if you are a beginner with no SEO experience. My name is Dorel Tănase and in the following minutes, I will show you a simple, step-by-step system that works even now. This is not about temporary tricks or risky tactics, but about clear, tested methods that help websites get consistent traffic from Google.

What is SEO!

If you are new to SEO, it's normal for everything to seem confusing and to wonder "What is SEO?". There are hundreds of guides, thousands of articles and many different opinions about what SEO is. Some say you need long content, others say links are everything, while others claim SEO is dead. The reality is much simpler. SEO essentially means three things:

  • create content that people search for,
  • show the Google search engine that this content is trustworthy,
  • provide a good experience to users who reach your website.

If you understand these three elements and apply them correctly, you can get results, even without a large budget. The first step is to understand what people are searching for. It's not enough to write about topics that seem interesting to you. You need to know exactly what expressions users type into Google. This is called keyword research.

Promotion tools

To start, you don't need complicated or expensive tools. You can use Google itself. Start typing a word in the search bar and observe the suggestions displayed automatically. These suggestions represent real searches made by people. For example, if you type "SEO", you will see suggestions like "SEO for beginners", "What is SEO", "SEO Google" or "SEO optimization". These are topics that people actually search for. The next step is to check the results displayed in Google for these searches. Analyze the top results and observe what type of content appears. Are they long articles? Are they step-by-step guides? Are they commercial pages? Google already shows you what it prefers for each type of search. Your role is to create better content than what already exists.

User intent

An important aspect is user intent. You need to understand why someone searches for that term. Do they want information? Do they want to buy something? Do they want a comparison? If you don't respect user intent, your content won't have results, no matter how well it's optimized. After you've chosen a topic and a keyword, the next step is creating the content. This is where most beginners make mistakes. Many write short, general articles that don't provide real value. To have a chance of reaching the first position, the content must be complete, clear and useful. It must answer all the questions a user might have related to that topic. It's not just about text length, but about how well it covers the topic. A good article explains things step by step, provides examples and is easy to understand.

Page structure

After you've chosen the right topic and created complete content, the next step is page structure. Structure is extremely important, both for users and for Google. First, the page title must be clear and include the main searched expression. This is the title that appears in Google results. If the title is not attractive or doesn't clearly explain what the user will find, people won't click, even if you are well positioned. A good title promises a clear benefit. For example, instead of a vague title, it's much more effective to specify exactly what the user will learn. Then, the content must be divided into logical sections, using titles and subtitles. This helps Google understand the information structure and helps readers navigate the page more easily. A well-structured article is easier to read, and users spend more time on the page. This is a positive signal for Google.

How do we create the introduction text?

Another important element is the introduction. The first lines must confirm to the user that they have arrived exactly where they need to be. If the introduction is too general or doesn't quickly answer the user's question, many will leave the page. After structure, comes on-page optimization. This is not about stuffing text with keywords. This practice no longer works and can even be harmful. The main keyword must appear naturally in the title, introduction and in a few subtitles, where it's logical. Google is smart enough to understand synonyms and context.

Relevant images in content

Also, it's important to include relevant images. Images help with content understanding and improve user experience. Each image should have a clear description, so Google knows what it's about. Another essential aspect is website speed. If the page loads slowly, users will leave, and Google will notice this behavior. A fast website provides a better experience and has higher chances of ranking well. After the content is published, many beginners think the work is done. In reality, this is just the beginning. A new article needs time to be evaluated by Google. During this period, it's important to promote it. One of the simplest things you can do is add internal links.

Internal links

Internal links are connections from other pages of your website to the new article. These help Google discover content faster and understand its importance. Also, internal links help users find relevant information more easily and stay longer on the website. One of the most important ranking factors in Google remains external links. Even though SEO has evolved a lot, links are still a strong trust signal. Think of links as recommendations. When a website refers to your content, it basically tells Google that page deserves attention. The more these recommendations come from relevant and trustworthy websites, the greater the impact. Not all links are equal. A single link from an authoritative website can have more value than dozens of low-quality links. That's why it's not recommended to try to get links quickly from dubious sources. For beginners, the best strategy is to create content so good that other people want to mention it. Detailed guides, case studies and articles that solve real problems have the highest chances of getting natural links. A simple method is to analyze what type of content already gets links in your niche. Look for popular articles, see what topics are mentioned frequently and create a better, more updated and easier to understand version.

Link diversity

Another important aspect is link diversity. It's much healthier to have links from several different sources, than many links from a single website. Also, the link text matters. It's good for links to be natural and varied. Google can identify artificial patterns, and these can reduce the impact of links. Besides links, Google analyzes how users interact with your page. If people enter the website and leave immediately, this is a negative signal. If they stay, read and navigate to other pages, it's a positive signal. That's why it's important to always think about user experience. A clear design, easy-to-read texts and a logical structure make the difference.

Content updating

Another essential thing is content updating. Google prefers pages that remain relevant over time. If you have an important article, return to it periodically, add new information and remove what's no longer valid. SEO is not a quick process. Results appear over time, but they are stable. If you follow these steps and have patience, you can build a website that attracts consistent traffic from Google. One of the most important things you need to understand about SEO is that results don't appear overnight. Many beginners give up too early, because they don't see immediate results. SEO is a process that requires time, consistency and patience. Generally, it can take several months before a new website starts to see clear results in Google. This is normal. Google needs time to evaluate content, links and user behavior. That's why it's important to have realistic expectations. SEO is not a quick solution, but it's one of the most stable sources of long-term traffic. A common mistake is to focus only on tricks or shortcuts. These may work short-term, but can lead to serious problems long-term. It's much safer to build things correctly from the beginning.

Regular content publishing

Another important thing is consistency. Regular publishing of quality content helps build website authority. You don't need to publish daily, but it's important to have a constant rhythm. Also, results analysis is essential. Track which pages perform well, what keywords bring traffic and where you can improve. SEO means continuous testing, adjustment and optimization. Finally, don't forget that the end goal is the user. Google wants to provide the best results for people. If you focus on creating useful, clear and easy-to-use content, Google will notice this. If you're a beginner, focus on the basics:

  1. choose searched topics,
  2. create valuable content,
  3. structure pages correctly,
  4. build quality links,
  5. constantly improve user experience.

If you follow these steps, you have real chances to reach the first position in Google, even as a beginner.
